concerns: Primary support is indirect (MISEV recommends orthogonal characterization and notes processing sensitivity) rather than a direct demonstration of the specific TFF parameter causality claimed.

Assay-interference and capture-reagent incompatibility are plausible alternative explanations; success depends on validated spike-in tracers and capture-compatibility panels (which are listed as dependencies but not yet demonstrated).
Manufacturability risk: lowered TMP/flux and added prefilters could reduce recovery/yield below acceptable thresholds—proposal acknowledges this but lacks prior yield data at scale-proxy conditions.

Translational gap: even if identity is preserved in vitro, ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution indicates species/route-specific clearance may still prevent downstream in vivo detectability; bridging in vivo recoverability tests are required.
Upstream variability (source-cell lot differences) could dominate signature loss; the experiment depends critically on availability of >=3 matched lots and on controlling upstream variability.
conclusion: The proposal is plausibly grounded in the cited ISEV guideline (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) and appropriately uses non-deliverability biodistribution data (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution) as a translational caution. The core inference—that lower per-cassette TMP/flux plus gentle prefiltration and cassette sequencing may preserve orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures—is supported indirectly by MISEV2023 guidance about processing sensitivity and the need for orthogonal characterization, but there is no direct published experimental evidence that the specific TFF envelope changes proposed causally prevent membrane damage or epitope masking at scale. The proposal correctly identifies necessary controls (spike-in, buffer compatibility) and designs experiments to distinguish assay artifacts from true damage. Key gaps remain: direct causal demonstration that high-TMP/high-flux TFF induces membrane-protection loss under scale-proxy conditions, and bridging evidence that preserved orthogonal signatures translate to improved in vivo detectability or functional comparability across species.
evidence_gap: No direct experimental evidence in the canonical set demonstrates that the proposed staged low-shear TFF envelope causally preserves membrane integrity/epitope exposure relative to high-flux TFF at scale-proxy volumes; additionally, there is no evidence linking preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature to improved in vivo detectability or functional outcomes across species.
